reading.body:
The DC BLOX Myrtle Beach Cable Landing Station sits at 1401 Howard Road in Myrtle Beach, South Carolina, but the operator publishes no power capacity, square footage, or IT load specification for this individual facility. The facility is named for cable landing infrastructure, which typically indicates direct subsea fiber connectivity rather than regional network access alone. Without facility-level watts published, its role in DC BLOX's footprint cannot be sized against the company's 470 critical MW across 23 facilities nationwide.

South Carolina has 14 mapped data center facilities, of which 4 publish power figures totaling 6.6 MW. This facility ranks fifth by published capacity in the state, though that ranking reflects only the four facilities that disclose watts at all, leaving the majority of mapped capacity opaque. The state's published supply remains minimal relative to national AI infrastructure scaling.

The Myrtle Beach location's cable landing designation suggests it functions as a network node or gateway rather than a primary compute campus. Without published power, the facility cannot be assessed for AI workload hosting capacity. Any evaluation of its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling depends on DC BLOX releasing facility-level specifications the operator has not yet made public.
